documentKindsNote: Each entry is a CATEGORY, a colon, then two or three worn examples of it separated by semicolons. The examples are spent: the linter (rule seeded-kind) fails a fragment title or source that carries one of them word for word. Write a fourth example of the category, in this world's own nouns.
documentKinds: writing sent to somebody who is not at work: letters home to a named relative; postcards written and never posted; a note folded into a parcel going out
words left for whoever is in the room next: notes for the next shift; a message chalked up by the kettle; a handover written on the back of something else
writing on the things themselves: labels and tags tied to objects; maintenance stickers stuck on the machines; a name inked inside a lid
a board or a card rewritten every day: the day's menu chalked up; a notice board nobody clears; a duty card with names crossed out
somebody else's words taken down by a listener: things said aloud and written down after; a speech with crossings-out; a quotation repeated in a letter
a child's writing, done on the premises: a school exercise book; a letter counting sleeps to something; homework marked by a parent at work
a tally somebody keeps for themselves: betting slips and a running total; a slate of tabs and who owes; a scorebook for a game played on breaks
instructions written for one particular person: how to look after an animal or a plant; how to work an awkward machine; what to say if a named person asks
a notebook carried in a pocket: a diary nobody else was meant to read; a list of grievances never handed in; a shopping list with prices and second thoughts
verses, songs and rhymes made up on the job: a work song added to by whoever was there; a rhyme painted where it can be read; a joke about the foreman that scans
writing on a wall that gets an answer under it: graffiti with replies added; a queue of signatures; days scratched in a column beside a door
writing about food: recipe cards with remarks; a tea rota with complaints on it; a note on what is in the cold store and whose it is
cards passed round a room and signed: birthday and leaving cards signed by everyone; a get-well card passed round a floor; a collection envelope with names and amounts
a form or a test filled in by the wrong person: a training quiz answered by a new starter; a questionnaire with one honest answer; an application never sent
margin notes in a book kept for work: corrections in an operating manual; a recipe book argued with in pencil; a catalogue with prices crossed out
calendars: days counted from the opening of the place (a three- or four-digit day number of your choosing)
ordinary dates: a day and a month, with clock times
shift numbers and a letter for the watch
the season and year of a contract or lease
voyage or campaign days, low numbers
batch or run numbers instead of dates
market days or pay days counted in a year
